newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria rejects U.S., Israeli peace proposals.
newsitem.headline: Syria rejects U.S., Israeli peace proposals.

text.p: Syria said on Thursday it would reject new U.S.-Israeli proposals to restart peace talks with Damascus, suspended since the election of hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in May.
Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara said Syria would not agree to fresh talks with Israel unless it honoured all the understandings reached with the previous government under Yitzhak Rabin.
"There are no new chapters in negotiations. There are commitments and pledges which should be honoured. Any other formula is a return to the zero point and this is not acceptable to us in Syria."
The foreign minister did not specify whether Damascus had received the proposals prepared by the United States and Israel to jump-start the peace process.

Speaking to reporters in Damascus together with his visiting Lebanese counterpart Faris Bouez, Shara accused Netanyahu of trying to mislead world public opinion by portraying Syria as the party rejecting calls for peace.

"Syria said several times that it was ready to resume the negotiations from the point where they stopped and on the principle of land for peace. Any other formula clearly shows that Israel does not want peace," he said.

U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Wednesday after talks between Netanyahu and U.S. leaders that Washington and Israel had developed proposals for restarting peace talks with Syria. He said the proposals had been passed on to Damascus.

Burns said U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross had long talks on the subject with Dore Gold, a key adviser to Netanyahu, after the Israeli leader met President Bill Clinton on Monday. Ross may travel to the Middle East next week, U.S. officials said.
In five years of sporadic talks, Syria has insisted that only a full Israeli withdrawal from the Golan Heights captured in the 1967 Middle East war would open the door to peace.
Netanyahu, who ousted Labour Party leader Shimon Peres in a national election last May, wants to keep the strategic plateau in Israeli hands.

He has called on Syria to renew talks unconditionally, although a report on Israel's Channel Two television said on Wednesday that Netanyahu was ready to accept some of the understandings reached by the government he toppled.

Peres and slain prime minister Yitzhak Rabin had agreed in talks with Arab partners to the principle of exchanging land for peace, but said the extent of Israel's withdrawal depended on Syria's readiness for normalisation.
